facts.raw_span: An 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma (cT1N0M0)
was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
new bilateral infiltrative shadows
He reported fever and dyspnea
elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative

Serologic testing for anti–nuclear antigen, anti–aminoacyl–tRNA synthetase, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide, anti-Sjögren’s-syndrome-related antigen A and B, and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antigen antibodies were all negative
no history of antigen exposure
grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis was suspected
bronchoscopy showed no airway secretions
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages, and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33

concepts.why: The patient developed new bilateral infiltrative shadows and symptoms after treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis was consistent with pneumonitis.
The patient's pneumonitis did not improve with steroid treatment, and bronchoscopy and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed persistent inflammation.
The patient was diagnosed with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, which is a type of cancer that affects the lining of the lungs.
The patient presented with fever and dyspnea, which are common symptoms of pneumonia, but negative sputum cultures and procalcitonin levels make this diagnosis less likely.

concepts.preferred_label: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
concepts.why: The patient had negative serologic testing for various connective tissue diseases, making this diagnosis less likely.
The patient had no history of antigen exposure, making this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's imaging and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed findings consistent with interstitial pneumonia, but the exact cause is unclear.
The patient's bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a high percentage of lymphocytes, which is consistent with lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia.
The patient's bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a significant percentage of neutrophils, which is consistent with neutrophilic interstitial pneumonia.
The patient's imaging and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed findings consistent with organizing pneumonia, but the exact cause is unclear.

rationales.F01: Epithelioid pleural mesothelioma is a known primary malignancy.
rationales.F02: Immune checkpoint inhibitors are known to cause pneumonitis.
rationales.F03: New bilateral infiltrative shadows are a common finding in pneumonitis.
rationales.F05: Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels are indicative of inflammation.
rationales.F08: Negative serologic testing helps rule out connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease.
rationales.F10: Grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis is a severe form of the disease.
rationales.F12: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis is helpful in diagnosing pneumonitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab, developed new bilateral infiltrative shadows, and had a poor response to steroid treatment, which supports the diagnosis of steroid-refractory immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis.
